speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The improvement in your psychiatric symptoms suggests the risperidone is working well, but we need to address the new movement disorder. How would you describe the involuntary movements you are experiencing, and do they affect your ability to perform daily tasks?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: These symptoms of an inability to sit still and repetitive leg movements are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent start on risperidone, this is a likely side effect. Have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or feeling like your muscles are cramping as well?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your history; the lack of substance use supports a medication-induced etiology. To further differentiate between akathisia and other extrapyramidal symptoms, have you noticed any muscle stiffness, jaw clenching, or tongue protrusion? REQUEST TEST: Drug_Levels_Risperidone

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those results; the absence of rigidity, bradykinesia, or dystonia (such as jaw clenching or tongue protrusion) further rules out Parkinsonism and acute dystonia. Based on the combination of restlessness, fidgeting, and your history with risperidone, the clinical picture strongly points to drug-induced akathisia. We do not need further imaging or lab tests to confirm this. DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia
